title: Cosmic Strings and Topological Defects
bottleneck: Phase transitions in the early universe should have produced cosmic strings or other defects in many particle theories, yet CMB and pulsar-timing data show no sign of them. Bounds on string tension keep tightening, but the allowed window for light strings persists, and a detection would be a direct fossil of GUT-scale physics. Strings would source a stochastic gravitational-wave background with a distinctive spectrum, offering a detection channel independent of the CMB.
why_it_blocks: Cosmic strings are one of few potential direct probes of energy scales 10 orders beyond colliders.
current_state: NANOGrav's gravitational-wave background could hide a string contribution, but astrophysical supermassive-black-hole binaries are the favored explanation. Current pulsar-timing data constrain but do not exclude light strings, leaving a discovery window open.
